Since $10^{726} \equiv 0 \pmod{1000}$, we have $727N = 10^{726}-1 \equiv -1 \pmod{1000}$. Because $\gcd(727,1000)=1$, $N \equiv -727^{-1} \pmod{1000}$.

Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, $245\cdot 1000 - 337\cdot 727 = 1$, so $727 \cdot (-337) \equiv 1 \pmod{1000}$. Thus $727^{-1} \equiv -337 \equiv 663 \pmod{1000}$, and $N \equiv -663 \equiv 337 \pmod{1000}$.
